cause: rollout granularity. n_envs 32 x n_steps 128 = 4096 env steps per PPO update. 1,000,000 / 4096 = 244.14, so the trainer completes update 245 rather than truncating mid-rollout. 245 x 4096 = 1,003,520.
classification: EXECUTION GRANULARITY, not a budget violation or an extension
why_it_is_not_an_extension: the overshoot is a property of the fixed rollout size, decided before launch, not a decision made after seeing results
no checkpoint was written at 1,000,000 that was then continued -- there is exactly one checkpoint, written at the end of update 245
the run was never inspected, paused, or resumed; it ran untouched to completion
truncating mid-rollout would have produced a partial update whose gradient was computed on fewer transitions than every other update in the run
note: 999,424 was the nearest under-budget alternative. Neither lands exactly on 1,000,000, because 1,000,000 is not a multiple of 4096. The protocol's 'exactly 1M' should be read as the declared budget, realised to the nearest whole rollout.
recommended_reporting: report 1,003,520 realised steps (245 PPO updates) with this note, not '1M' unqualified
applies_equally_to: the development sweep, where 98,304 = 24 x 4096 happens to be an exact multiple and so showed no overshoot
